primary_link.title: RASFT: Rollout-Adaptive Supervised Fine-Tuning for Reasoning

papers.summary: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is a prevailing method for adapting large language models to reasoning tasks by imitating offline expert demonstrations, often treating a single expert trajectory as the target behavior. However, reasoning is not simple path imitation: rigidly following one demonstrated solution may overfit to surface forms and suppress the model's own reasoning distribution. We propose Rollout-Adaptive Supervised Fine-Tuning (RASFT), a policy-aware SFT framework that calibrates expe
papers.summary_zh: 監督式微調 (SFT) 是透過模仿離線專家示範來調整大型語言模型以適應推理任務的主流方法，但往往將單一專家軌跡視為目標行為，忽略了推理並非簡單的路徑模仿。為了克服嚴格遵循單一解題路徑可能導致的表層過擬合與對模型自身推理分佈的抑制，本文提出了 Rollout-Adaptive Supervised Fine-Tuning (RASFT)。此框架引入了策略感知機制，能夠動態校正專家示範。值得關注的是，RASFT 在提升模型推理泛化能力的同時，也保留了 SFT 的訓練效率，為增強推理模型的穩健性提供了新思路。

papers.title_zh: RASFT：面向推理的滾動適應性監督式微調

papers.summary_zh: 推理型大型語言模型可透過審慎推論來提升解題效能，但對所有輸入都啟動慢速推理不僅計算成本高昂，且往往不必要。針對此問題，本文提出 IDPR 框架，該框架首先生成一個簡潔的直覺答案，再透過抑制控制器決定是直接輸出該回應，還是抑制它以啟動更耗時的慢速推理。與傳統僅根據輸入進行判斷的路由器不同，IDPR 的抑制機制還考慮了當前生成回應的品質。此方法旨在計算資源與推理深度之間取得更智慧的平衡，有望在實際應用中顯著提升效率。

primary_link.title: Signal-Driven Observation for Long-Horizon Web Agents

papers.summary: Web agents operating over long horizons ingest raw DOM and accessibility trees -- routinely tens of thousands of tokens -- at every action step, causing progressive context degradation that erodes reasoning well before tasks complete. We argue that this coupling of observation frequency to action frequency is an architectural mistake. Drawing on the insight from Recursive Language Models that querying a document outperforms reading it wholesale, we propose Signal-Driven Observation (SDO): a dedi
papers.summary_zh: 在長時間範圍內運作的網頁代理，每個動作步驟都需要處理包含數萬個 token 的原始 DOM 與無障礙樹，這導致上下文逐步退化，並在任務完成前就削弱了模型的推理能力。本文認為將觀測頻率與動作頻率耦合是一種架構性錯誤，並借鑒遞歸式語言模型中「查詢文件優於通讀全文」的見解，提出了 Signal-Driven Observation (SDO)。此方法引入一個專用觀測策略來決定何時以及如何進行詳細觀察，而非機械式地在每一步驟都讀取完整頁面。作者主張 SDO 能有效緩解上下文退化問題，顯著提升長時程網頁任務的完成率與推理品質。
papers.title: Signal-Driven Observation for Long-Horizon Web Agents
papers.title_zh: 訊號驅動觀測：面向長時程網頁代理的決策框架

links.title: Double Preconditioning (DoPr): Optimization for Test-Time Performance, not Validation Loss

primary_link.title: Double Preconditioning (DoPr): Optimization for Test-Time Performance, not Validation Loss

papers.summary: Many modern applications of deep learning involve training a neural network via a one-step prediction loss (e.g., $L^2$ regression, cross-entropy), but deploy the network by rolling out along its own predictions. Key examples include autoregressive language modeling, flow-based generative modeling, and robot policy learning. It is well-documented that these settings induce a phenomenon we call test-time feedback (TTF): the mismatch between the training/validation loss and downstream metrics of i
papers.summary_zh: 許多現代深度學習的應用是透過一步式預測損失（如 L² 回歸或交叉熵）來訓練神經網路，但在部署時卻是讓網路根據自身的預測進行滾動推論。典型例子包括自迴歸語言模型、基於流的生成模型以及機器人策略學習。本文指出此設定會引發「測試時反饋 (TTF)」現象，即訓練/驗證損失與下游任務指標之間存在嚴重不匹配。為此，作者提出了 Double Preconditioning (DoPr) 方法，透過在訓練過程中引入雙重預處理機制，直接針對測試時的性能進行最佳化。此方法的核心貢獻在於彌合了訓練目標與實際部署目標之間的鴻溝，為提升模型在滾動推論場景下的最終表現提供了有效途徑。
papers.title: Double Preconditioning (DoPr): Optimization for Test-Time Performance, not Validation Loss
papers.title_zh: 雙重預處理 (DoPr)：針對測試時性能而非驗證損失的最佳化

links.title: Subspace-Aware Sparse Autoencoders for Effective Mechanistic Interpretability

primary_link.title: Subspace-Aware Sparse Autoencoders for Effective Mechanistic Interpretability

papers.summary: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) are widely used for mechanistic interpretability in large language models, yet their formulation assigns each latent feature a single decoder direction, implicitly assuming features to be one-dimensional. papers.summary_zh: 大型語言模型在推論時通常遵循固定的深度與順序，即非遞迴地執行所有層。本文揭示了訓練後、靈活且動態的程式化層級結構的廣泛存在，其中預訓練的層可以被封裝為模組，並根據每個輸入的特定需求被跳過或循環，以形成客製化的程式。對於大多數輸入，採用更短的程式執行可以達到相同甚至更高的準確率；同時，原始 LLM 的錯誤預測也能透過這種動態調整得到修正。此發現挑戰了傳統的固定前饋推論範式，為未來 LLM 架構的設計提供了全新思路。

papers.summary: Scientific paper recommendation is typically evaluated as static ranking over a fixed candidate set, yet real scientific reading unfolds as a daily, longitudinal process in which interests shift and feedback accumulates. primary_link.title: Socratic-SWE: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Trace-Derived Agent Skills

top5.summary: LLM-driven software engineering agents have become a central testbed for real-world language-model capability, yet their training remains limited by the availability of high-quality SWE tasks. Existing synthetic data methods typically create tasks through fixed mutation or bug-injection procedures, making the resulting distributions largely independent of the agent's own weaknesses and training progress. We introduce Socratic-SWE, a closed-loop self-evolution framework that reuses the agent's historical solving traces as a source of training signal. Rather than treating traces only as evidence for reward computation, Socratic-SWE distills them into structured agent skills that summarize recurring failures and effective repair patterns. These skills then guide the generation of targeted repair tasks in real repositories. Candidate tasks are checked through execution-based validation and scored with a solver-gradient alignment reward, so that the retained tasks are both verifiable and useful for improving the Solver. The updated Solver produces new traces, enabling the task curriculum to adapt over successive rounds. Across SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Lite, SWE-bench Pro, and Terminal-Bench 2.0, Socratic-SWE consistently improves over self-evolving baselines under the same compute budget, reaching 50.40% on SWE-bench Verified after three iterations. links.title: Your UnEmbedding Matrix is Secretly a Feature Lens for Text Embeddings

primary_link.title: Your UnEmbedding Matrix is Secretly a Feature Lens for Text Embeddings

top5.summary: Large language models exhibit impressive zero-shot capabilities across a wide range of downstream tasks. However, they struggle to function as off-the-shelf embedding models, leading to suboptimal performance on massive text embedding benchmarks. In this paper, we identify a potential cause underlying this deficiency. Our motivation stems from an unexpected observation: text embeddings tend to align with frequent but uninformative tokens when projected onto the vocabulary space. We argue that this excessive expression of high-frequency tokens suppresses the model's ability to capture nuanced semantics. To address this, we introduce EmbedFilter, a simple linear transformation designed to refine text embeddings derived from LLMs directly. Specifically, we uncover that the unembedding matrix within LLMs encodes a latent space that is actively writing these frequent tokens into embedding space. By filtering out this subspace, EmbedFilter suppress the influence of high-frequency tokens, thereby enhancing semantic representations. As a compelling byproduct, this enables an inherent dimensionality reduction, lowering index storage and speedup retrieval while fully preserving the refined embedding quality. Our experiments across multiple LLM backbones demonstrate that LLMs equipped with EmbedFilter achieve superior zero-shot downstream performance even with significantly reduced embedding dimensions. We hope our findings provide deeper insights into the mechanisms of LLM-based representations and inspire more principled designs to improve text embeddings training. Our code is available at https://github.com/CentreChen/EmbFilter.
